title: Former TikTok Star Ali Abulaban Seeks New Trial for Double Murder
text:
Former TikTok Star Ali Abulaban Seeks New Trial Following Double Murder Conviction in San Diego The Tech TL;DR: Case Status: Ali Abulaban was sentenced to two consecutive 25-year-to-life terms in prison without the possibility of rehabilitation. Legal Appeal: The defense petitioned for a mistrial during sentencing, citing allegedly improper prosecution questioning regarding a courtroom outburst. Court Ruling: San Diego Superior Court Judge Jeffrey Fraser rejected the motion, ruling that the trial proceedings remained uncompromised by the incident. Case Background and Legal Proceedings at the Spire San Diego According to coverage by NBC San Diego , the murders occurred at the Spire San Diego luxury apartment complex. Abulaban admitted during trial to killing Ana Abulaban, 28, and Rayburn Cardenas Barron, 29. San Diego Superior Court Judge Jeffrey Fraser sentenced Abulaban, 32, to two consecutive 25-year-to-life prison terms.
During the sentencing hearing, Judge Fraser addressed the defendant directly, stating that he held “serious reservations” regarding any claims of remorse. According to court statements cited by NBC San Diego, the judge remarked, “The bottom line here is, he will die in prison, he will never be a free man. He will take his last breath there.” Fraser also characterized Abulaban as a “very talented actor,” comparing his demeanor during the killings to the cinematic persona of Scarface.
Defense Arguments and Prosecution Line of Questioning Prior to formal sentencing, the defense team argued for a retrial based on specific lines of questioning pursued by the prosecution. According to court records, the questioning had previously prompted a verbal outburst from Abulaban during the trial proceedings. Although the judge had earlier ruled that the specific lines of inquiry could be stricken from the record for the jury, the defense maintained that the exchange fundamentally tainted the jury’s perspective, warranting a mistrial.
Judge Fraser rejected the appeal, determining that the contested moment did not prejudice the outcome. During the hearing, Abulaban addressed the court by reading from yellow, lined paper, apologizing for the pain inflicted on both families while attempting to characterize his actions as a crime of passion stemming from what he described as a “drug-induced psychosis.” Abulaban also expressed concern over the duration of his testimony relative to the jury’s deliberation timeline.
Impact Statements and Courtroom Testimony The sentencing hearing featured victim impact statements delivered by six loved ones of Ana Abulaban and Rayburn Cardenas Barron. Ana Abulaban’s sister addressed the defendant directly regarding past abuse and family support structures in the Philippines. Barron’s family members described him as a dedicated family man committed to assisting others, noting the profound psychological and emotional toll the tragedy has inflicted on their relatives.
